gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-general-sans: Expressive and loose, Balsamiq Sans draws its lines like channels cut through a stencil, never pinching a curve. General Sans keeps going once the heading is done, its lowercase filling the line so a long passage moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-orbit: Orbit handles the body with rounded characters that float apart from each other, curves stopping short of closing. Balsamiq Sans is the one with the bold, stencil-cut swagger for headings.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-syncopate: Bold, stencil-like Balsamiq Sans carries the heading with no pinched curves, while Syncopate spaces its open shapes like rungs on a ladder. Made small, the heading loses its swagger.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-manrope: Manrope leaves a bright gap at the mouth of every curve, and its capitals barely step up from the lowercase. Balsamiq Sans then adds its stencil-cut boldness, and a long passage would read smoothly in that single-width line.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-switzer: Approachable Switzer builds wire-like letters with c tips that never creep toward touching, set against the bold stencil-cut channels of Balsamiq Sans. Paragraphs read crisp and light.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-work-sans: Work Sans sets its mean line high and keeps its c tips from creeping toward touching, which gives the body a modern lift. Balsamiq Sans is best at bold, pinch-free headings; Work Sans is best at plain, steady text.
gen-gf-baumans-archivo: A crescent-wrench c, opened wide, marks Baumans, and every stroke is drawn at one thickness under that heading. Archivo follows in sans-serif form, its curves opening outward so long text reads with ease.
gen-gf-baumans-fs-merriweather-sans: Baumans leads with a crescent-wrench c and no tilt in its round letters. Its strongest trait is the contrast with Merriweather Sans, whose big, sturdy lowercase and open e feel like a different voice.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-science-gothic: Baumans opens with a commanding crescent-wrench c. Its best quality is the contrast with Science Gothic, whose stroke ends sit far apart and whose letters have no thick or thin parts, so each is read one at a time.
gen-gf-baumans-switzer: Wrench-shaped and bold, that c sets the heading apart. Baumans commands the top line with uniform strokes, while Switzer takes over below with wire-like sans letters whose generous lowercase keeps text open and approachable.
